messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant that solves tasks step by step.

Task Guide:

Simulate uniaxial tensile loading of an Aluminum single crystal using LAMMPS. The crystal should be oriented such that the simulation box axes x, y, and z align with the crystallographic <100> directions of the face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice. Use metal units and define an FCC lattice with a lattice constant of 4.05 Å. Construct a 10×10×10 unit cell simulation box with periodic boundary conditions in all directions. Employ the Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potential for Aluminum. Equilibrate the system at 300 K and zero pressure isotropically using the NPT ensemble with a Nose-Hoover thermostat and barostat. Use a timestep of 0.001 picoseconds and run equilibration for at least 20 picoseconds. Following equilibration, apply uniaxial tensile deformation along the x-axis at a strain rate of 0.01 ps⁻¹ by deforming the simulation box in the x-direction, while maintaining zero pressure in the transverse y and z directions via NPT dynamics. Continue deformation for 20 picoseconds to capture the material’s mechanical response. Record the strain and corresponding stress components in the format `strain, stress_xx, stress_yy, stress_zz` every 100 timesteps, with stresses saved in GPa. As the final result, report the maximum tensile stress (in GPa) along the x-direction achieved prior to the onset of plastic deformation or structural instability, identified as the first significant drop in the stress-strain response. This is a large simulation, hence it is advisable to use multiple CPUs. Make sure all the associated files for this task (input files, log files, any other files) are in the /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/tool_calling/claude_35/workflow/task_8/task_8_trial_2 directory. You can use the available I/O tools (e.g., write_file) make new files .etc. Whatever potentials you need to run the simulation, you can find them at /potentials/. A type of potential can be accessed by /potentials/TYPE where TYPE can be [EAM, TERSOFF, REAXFF] which further contains the exact potential files. Note that in case of reaxff potentials, pair style 'reax/c' has been renamed to 'reaxff' and always use NULL for the control file (cfile), for example, this syntax is correct : pair_style reaxff NULL. If the task is to give the final output as a scalar, only return the numerical value, without any units.

You must think what to do next. You can use some of the tools available in the system.

When you think that the task is completed, you can submit the answer.
For that, answer with: "Final Answer: <your answer>". It is very important to follow this format.

I'll help you solve this task step by step.

{"path": "/results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/tool_calling/claude_35/workflow/task_8/task_8_trial_2/tensile.in", "content": "units metal
dimension 3
boundary p p p
atom_style atomic

# Create FCC lattice
lattice fcc 4.05
region box block 0 10 0 10 0 10
create_box 1 box
create_atoms 1 box
mass 1 26.98

# Define potential
pair_style eam/alloy
pair_coeff * * /potentials/EAM/Al_zhou.eam.alloy Al

# Energy minimization
minimize 1.0e-6 1.0e-8 1000 10000

# Define temperature and timestep
timestep 0.001
velocity all create 300.0 12345

# Equilibration in NPT
fix 1 all npt temp 300.0 300.0 0.1 iso 0.0 0.0 1.0
thermo 1000
run 20000

unfix 1

# Reset time step counter
reset_timestep 0

# Tensile deformation
fix 1 all npt temp 300.0 300.0 0.1 y 0.0 0.0 1.0 z 0.0 0.0 1.0
fix 2 all deform 1 x erate 0.01 units box remap x

# Output settings
variable strain equal "(lx - v_L0)/v_L0"
variable L0 equal ${lx}
variable stress_xx equal -pxx/10000  # Convert to GPa
variable stress_yy equal -pyy/10000
variable stress_zz equal -pzz/10000

fix stress_output all print 100 "${strain} ${stress_xx} ${stress_yy} ${stress_zz}" file stress_strain.txt screen no

# Run deformation
run 20000"}
